subject: Pre-sales: token burst heatmap + sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing data: token burst heatmap and traces

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier — following up with the raw traces we promised. Attaching a token-level heatmap CSV (acme_token_heatmap.csv) and a small sample of customer prompts (acme_sample_prompts.json). Quick summary of what you’ll see:

- Daily peak around 11:00–11:20 PDT (corresponds to a marketing batch) with short bursts: median burst window ~90s, top bursts up to ~14k tokens in the window.
- Prompt lengths: median ~95 tokens, 90th pct ~280 tokens. Response lengths: median ~160 tokens, 95th pct ~540 tokens.
- Session mix: ~65% conversational chat (multi-turn), ~25% single-shot generation, ~10% embedding/semantic search.
- Concurrency: baseline 40 concurrent sessions, burst P90 ~320 concurrent sessions, P99 ~680.
- Warm-up: traffic often ramps quickly after batch sends; KV-cache hit is ~55% after a 3–5 minute window.

We’ve also included a short SLA doc (acme_sla_requirements.pdf) — goal is p99 latency <= 180ms for the chat path and availability 99.9%. Please flag any obvious sizing concerns.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Product Ops | Acme AI
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data: token burst heatmap and traces

Sarah —

Appreciate the data, that heatmap and prompts are exactly what we need to start a conservative sizing pass. A few clarifying requests before we run the estimator and map to GPU SKUs:

1) Burst shape: the CSV looks like 60s buckets. Can you confirm whether the 14k top-window is a single 60s bucket spike or an aggregated multi-minute window?
2) Session affinity: do individual users persist to the same session/slot for their multi-turn flows, or are sessions evenly distributed each turn? (affects KV cache effectiveness)
3) Model variant: are you planning to serve a single LLM across both chat and single-shot, or will chat use a larger context/parameters model? If different, supply model names/approx sizes.
4) Tokenization: the sample prompts show mixed languages; please confirm if tokenization is GPT-style (we’ll assume bpe) or if you want us to run a test tokenize pass.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm (1)–(4) by EOD, we’ll produce a conservative and an aggressive capacity map (GPU mix + redundancy) tomorrow and propose a 30-min sync Friday to walk numbers.

Quick note: Marissa is our workload lead and will validate the KV-cache assumptions; Karthik will be the quantization/sku lead.

Thanks — I’ll slot a tentative Friday 11:00 PT on the calendar; let us know if that works.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Ops <ops@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data: token burst heatmap and traces

Hi Irene —

Answers inline below and attaching a slightly trimmed heatmap (same CSV format) to highlight the true per-minute peaks:

> 1) Burst shape: the CSV looks like 60s buckets. Can you confirm whether the 14k top-window is a single 60s bucket spike or an aggregated multi-minute window?

That 14k is a single 60s bucket (it came from a timed push notification campaign). We also see nearby spillover in the following 2–3 minutes but nothing that exceeds the 60s peak.

> 2) Session affinity: do individual users persist to the same session/slot for their multi-turn flows, or are sessions evenly distributed each turn?

Affinity is high: ~72% of active users maintain the same session slot for their conversation (cookies + sticky routing in our frontend). That’s why the KV cache numbers you saw are realistic.

> 3) Model variant: are you planning to serve a single LLM across both chat and single-shot, or will chat use a larger context/parameters model?

We plan to serve two variants: a 13B-ish chat-optimized model (chat path, longer context) and a 7B generation model for single-shot tasks. Both are quantized to int8 for cost reasons. We can provide model binaries if needed for detailed kernel-fit analysis.

> 4) Tokenization: the sample prompts show mixed languages; please confirm if tokenization is GPT-style (we’ll assume bpe) or if you want us to run a test tokenize pass.

We’re using a GPT-style BPE tokenizer across the board. If Redwood can run a tokenize pass to show per-variant token counts (post-normalization), that’d be helpful.

We’re good for the Friday 11:00 PT sync. Attaching: acme_token_heatmap_trimmed.csv (per-minute), acme_sample_prompts.json (10 examples), and the SLA PDF.

—Sarah
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data: token burst heatmap and traces

Perfect, thanks Sarah — this is clear and actionable. Next steps from our side:

- We’ll run a two-path sizing: (A) conservative map assuming 72% affinity + int8 13B/7B split; (B) aggressive map that plans for peak P99 concurrency (680) and 2x redundancy headroom. Expect a short write-up and GPU SKU mix by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik will run a quantized kernel-fit probe against the sample prompts to check latency p99 estimates.
- Marissa will validate cache warming assumptions and recommend runtime batching windows.

I’ve linked the HubSpot deal and added the heatmap to the shared Drive for your team. We’ll present the sizing options on Friday’s call and include a fallback routing policy if capacity is constrained.

See you Friday 11:00 PT — invite incoming.

Thanks,
Irene
